subject: Prefetch hop interference & H-O-L latency — leadership alert and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@fastretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaSInfraOps@fastretail.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:17:22 -0800
Subject: Sudden p99 spike + 500s after your Nov 23 rollout — need immediate help

Hi Jonas / Laura,

We started seeing a sharp P99 increase and rising 5xx rates in our production traffic within an hour of Redwood's Nov 23 runtime update. Throughput dropped ~25% on our busiest endpoints and a subset of requests are timing out (many are streaming requests). Attached are the logs and a short flamegraph from our side (production_logs_20261124.zip).

Preliminary notes from our ops team:
- The spikes look correlated with very large prefix churns (lots of unbound prefixes being prefetched then evicted).
- There are frequent KV cache evictions and a backlog forming on hot lanes; traces show head-of-line blocking where longer-running requests stall younger ones.
- Error pattern: transient 502/504 with retry storms from our client.

This is customer-impacting — checkout queues are timing out for a small percentage of users and our SLO alerts are firing across regions. We need a triage call today to get a mitigation plan and an ETA for a fix. If this requires a config rollback or emergency patch, tell us what you need.

Please advise on immediate mitigations and when your team can join.

Thanks,
Claire
SRE Lead, FastRetail

(Attachment: production_logs_20261124.zip)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:45:03 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike + 500s after your Nov 23 rollout — need immediate help

Hi Claire — thanks for the signal and for the logs. I'm taking point on this.

Immediate plan (first 90 minutes):
1) Triage call: 10:00 PT today — joining with SRE and CS.
2) Short-term mitigations we can push ASAP:
   - Reduce batch window (ms_timeout) from 12ms -> 6ms to lower HOL exposure and unblock the hot path.
   - Temporarily shrink max batch size from 16->8 for FastRetail routes to reduce tail latency amplification.
   - Bump KV cache reservation for pinned prefixes used by your checkout flows (pin top-500 prefixes) and set a higher eviction grace window.
3) If those don't stabilize within 30-60 minutes, we'll roll a targeted rollback of the recent kernel change tied to prefetch heuristics.

Marcus, can you validate whether we can make those config changes without a full restart? Laura, can you prepare an exec note and coordinate credits if this crosses our SLA threshold? Evelyn, please prepare CS comms and the postmortem template.

Claire — joining link for the triage call: https://zoom.redwood.com/meet/jw-triage-1124

Jonas
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Claire Huang <claire@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:08:41 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike + 500s after your Nov 23 rollout — need immediate help

On the triage call now — quick updates and proposed runbook steps I can execute immediately: 

Quick findings (from our side):
- The recent prefetch heuristics change introduced more aggressive prefix prefetch for long-tail keys; combined with your traffic mix this causes sustained cache churn.
- KV eviction rate jumped ~6x on affected nodes; hot-lane queue times spiked causing HOL blocking for streaming requests.

Immediate actions I'm applying (now):
- Reduce batch_window_ms to 6 on your tenant routes (no restart required, rolling config).
- Reduce max_batch_size to 8 for the next 60 minutes.
- Increase prefix_cache_reserve_pct from 10 -> 22 for pinned prefixes used by checkout flows.
- Enable short-circuit fallback: if a request waits > 120ms in queue, route to a compatible lighter-weight model variant.

I pushed the first two changes 10:12 PT and we're already seeing a partial p99 improvement (+/- 35% reduction). Will keep monitoring and post metrics. If stabilization fails in 45 mins we'll schedule a rollback of the prefetch kernel.

Attaching the mitigation playbook that codifies these steps (mitigation_playbook.md).

-Marcus
SRE, Redwood Inference

(Attachment: mitigation_playbook.md)
From: Claire Huang <claire@fastretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaSInfraOps@fastretail.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:02:09 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike + 500s after your Nov 23 rollout — need immediate help

Thanks Marcus / Jonas — we joined the call and see the same immediate improvement on our dashboards (p99 down ~30%). Appreciate the quick action.

Two asks from FastRetail:
1) Can you confirm a timeline for the rollback if the partial mitigations don't converge? Our peak traffic window is tonight at 20:00 PT.
2) We'll need a brief executive summary for our CTO and procurement; also want to discuss pro-rated credits if this meets an SLA breach.

We'll stay on the monitoring channel and will escalate if anything regresses.

Claire
SRE Lead, FastRetail
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@fastretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Incident update & exec briefing — prefetch-induced HOL interference

Follow-up and status for leadership and FastRetail: 

Summary: The root cause is an over-aggressive prefetch heuristic introduced in the Nov 23 runtime update that increased prefix churn for FastRetail's traffic pattern. That churn drove KV cache thrash and created head-of-line blocking on hot lanes, amplifying p99 tail latency and producing transient 502/504 responses.

What we did: 
- Short-term mitigations (Nov 24): reduced batch window and batch size, increased KV reserve for pinned prefixes, enabled short-circuit routing to lighter variants. These measures stabilized p99 by ~30% within the first hour.
- Medium-term: rolled back the prefetch heuristic for affected model families on Nov 25 at 02:00 PT (targeted rollback, no customer-facing downtime). Additional smoothing and monitoring were added to prefetch logic and we hardened eviction backpressure.
- Customer remediation: we are preparing a formal SLA assessment and will propose pro-rated credits if the incident qualifies. Laura is drafting the customer-facing executive note.

Next steps owned: 
- Marcus: run a 48-hour soak and monitor eviction/queue metrics; if any regressions occur, revert to conservative prefetch by default.
- Evelyn: postmortem and customer comms to ship within 72 hours.
- Laura: finalize exec note and credit proposal; loop in finance for approval.

For FastRetail: thank you for rapid coordination. Claire, let me know any additional asks for the CTO briefing. We'll share the postmortem and the timeline for improvements.

-Jonas
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
